A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal representation and sim-to-real transfer work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting changes and expanded experiments in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ORCA simulation experiments, causal-awareness and robustness evaluations, and ETH-UCY transfer results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and ETH-UCY experiments and adds NBA rebound, JRDB, and additional comparator results.

M1.justification: The projected cosine-distance representation, contrastive and ranking regularizers, and joint real-prediction/synthetic-causal objective remain unchanged in Equations 4–8. Additional backbone and multimodal experiments apply the existing framework; the PDFs do not establish a new regularizer or transfer procedure.

E1.justification: v2 extends real-world evaluation beyond ETH-UCY pedestrians to NBA rebound trajectories and JRDB human motion. It also removes the separately evaluated combined density-plus-context/plaza scenario, while retaining the individual density and context shifts.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Multi-Transmotion. The ETH-UCY model comparison removes EqMotion and adds ORCA and Social-Transmotion (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6). New Table 7 directly compares against AutoBots with causal intervention. These change the evaluated comparator sets, beyond extending existing comparisons to new datasets.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a held-out indoor/outdoor JRDB split and deterministic K=1 versus multimodal K=5 evaluation. Reported OOD-context composition also changes, including mean agents per scene from 29.01 to 21.39 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 10), without explaining whether this reflects regeneration or correction. The shared prediction horizon, metrics, and stated training recipe remain.

E4.justification: The robustness analysis loses the combined density/context stress test, and Figures 6 and 9 add ID forecasting results alongside the remaining shifts. The causal-effect quantile and category analyses remain. Figure 7 retains the same qualitative prediction examples in a different order.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds for the controlled simulation figures and three seeds for ETH-UCY stability results, retaining the standard-deviation discussion and best-of-three benchmark comparison. The added NBA and JRDB tables introduce no stated new uncertainty estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: The ETH-UCY transfer tables match numerically across versions. New results include NBA ranking ADE/FDE of 0.544/1.235 versus the AutoBots baseline's 0.562/1.271, and JRDB K=1 ADE of 0.342 versus Multi-Transmotion's 0.379. Table 1 gains a new prediction leader, and Figures 6, 9, and 10 contain revised results. These are additions and revisions, not established cross-version performance gains under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the non-causal, direct-causal, and indirect-causal category definitions retain the same mathematical substance. Expanded explanations of factual embeddings and individual-agent counterfactuals add no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The benchmark critique, causal regularization, and transfer without real-world causal annotations remain the central contributions. v2 makes the abstract's data-efficiency claim specific to using 25% of real-world data and broadens the stated empirical demonstration beyond pedestrians to basketball trajectories.

C2.justification: v2 uses ORCA's poor ETH-UCY forecasting performance to strengthen its interpretation that useful causal knowledge transfers despite the simulation gap. It removes v1's concluding caveat about predominantly simulation-based proof-of-concept evidence, while retaining the technical reasoning limitation and Appendix C's simulator-realism and group-causality caveats.

D1.justification: v2 changes the code pointer to the specific CausalSim2Real repository and explicitly states availability of the dataset and generation code. It adds details such as initialization with 8–18 agents and the deterministic simulator's single-trajectory output setting. The main hyperparameter table and ten-epoch fine-tuning description are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references associated with Multi-Transmotion, Social-Transmotion, JRDB, and NBA evaluation, while removing EqMotion and works cited in the deleted future-directions passage. The three-part related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged. The causal-intervention work was already cited in v1; its direct empirical comparison is new.

P1.justification: Most of the narrative and section sequence are retained. Local revisions clarify the benchmark caveats, embedding construction, and transfer explanation; Formalism becomes Preliminaries, Appendix A gains subsections, and Appendix D is added. Author order, affiliations, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The main paper and references switch from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 7's existing panels are reordered, and several plots change axes and displayed conditions. New NBA, intervention, and JRDB tables and the six-panel synthetic-data Figure 13 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: NBA and JRDB evaluations, an additional forecasting backbone, and the direct causal-intervention comparison broaden support beyond v1's ETH-UCY-only real-world evaluation. Clearer explanations and access information also help. These gains are limited by removal of the combined-shift stress test and EqMotion comparison, plus sparse protocol and uncertainty details for the new experiments. Overall, the evidence supports a modest net quality improvement.
